description: Required end-to-end coverage of one competition from creation to close. The lifecycle lane, the source check and the walkthrough verifier read this contract; change it only through review, never to make a run pass.

forbidden_patterns.reason: Actors must be ordinary role accounts; elevation hides access defects.
Policy bypass skips the review being tested.
Workflow state must change through commands, not writes.
Workflow state must change through commands, not assignment.
A skipped scenario is not evidence.

required_methods.name: test_league_runs_from_creation_to_closed_competition
required_methods.covers: Streamlined league: Create Competition wizard (league preset, 14/12 rule set) -> Select Teams -> Choose Format (single round robin) -> Define Game Days (two days, one venue, two courts) -> Plan Competition -> submit, approve and publish -> competition becomes Open, then In Progress when the first day opens -> one gameday roster per team, players crossed out per match -> court operator saves and submits every result -> approved results mark matches done -> linked league table updates without manual records -> each gameday closes without force -> table frozen -> Hub closes the competition -> public site lists it as Completed.

required_methods.name: test_independent_review_is_enforced_in_controlled_mode
required_methods.covers: Controlled workflow: the schedule planner cannot approve or publish their own schedule; the result submitter cannot verify or approve their own result; an independent approver can. Database state is unchanged after each denied command.

required_methods.name: test_tournament_day_runs_groups_then_knockout_from_one_publication
required_methods.covers: Tournament-day preset with groups then knockout: knockout fixtures with unknown teams are scheduled and published once; finishing the groups fills the knockout teams without republication; a tied knockout match progresses via resolution type and advancing team; the final placement is complete.

required_methods.name: test_correcting_a_progressed_result_rolls_back_the_next_round
required_methods.covers: Correcting a knockout result after the winner moved on withdraws the unplayed follow-up match with an audit event, refills it with the corrected winner, and refuses the correction once the follow-up has started.

required_methods.name: test_competition_cannot_close_while_work_is_unfinished
required_methods.covers: Closing reports every blocker (unfinished matches, open gamedays, unapproved results, unfrozen tables); the raw Close and Reset to Draft buttons are refused on the server; closing succeeds once the blockers are cleared.

required_methods.name: test_forfeit_and_bye_points_follow_the_rule_set
required_methods.covers: A forfeit recorded on court and a structural bye award the rule-set points (not the score) in the linked table.

required_methods.name: test_suspension_dates_and_match_count_control_eligibility
required_methods.covers: A future-dated suspension does not suspend the player until its start date (daily job); a match-count suspension expires after the team plays that many matches; a suspension issued after the gameday roster was approved blocks that player at match start.

required_methods.name: test_gameday_roster_limits_hold_through_result_submission
required_methods.covers: A 14-player gameday roster is shared by all matches that day; result submission is refused while more than 12 players are left playing; each match keeps its own crossed-out players.

walkthrough.description: Browser evidence on the disposable walkthrough server. Each step is performed through the real UI by the stated actor; mobile steps use a 390x844 viewport.

required_steps.expect: Create Competition wizard with the league preset creates the competition and opens the Competition Hub with one next action.
Select Teams finalizes the four seeded teams.
Choose Format shows the preview, requires confirmation and generates fixtures.
Define Game Days creates two days with event-local times.
Plan Competition assigns every fixture; submission, approval and publication succeed; the competition shows Open.
Portal shows one gameday roster per team and day, no starter selection, at most 14 players.
Players for this match accepts crossing out down to 12 and keeps different choices per match.
The official sees and accepts the assignment with event-local time.
Opening the first day moves the competition to In Progress.
Court workspace lists only participating players; save draft, submit and next match work; status distinguishes device, server, submitted and approved.
Approving results marks matches done and updates the public table.
Each finished gameday closes without forcing.
The Hub leads through freezing the table and closing the competition.
The public site lists the competition as Completed with the final table.
Crafted URLs for another club's roster, sheet and documents are refused and change nothing.
